examples.description: Inspired by the bright violet recruiting reference with a full application shell, compact KPI cards, stage-flow analysis, and a candidate work queue.
examples.expected: KPI totals, stage charts, gender mix, role demand, and candidate records render from one application-level dataset and cross-highlight by source row lineage.
examples.limitations: Profile photography is replaced by safe initials and bundled icons so the example remains offline and Power BI portable.
examples.summary: A polished recruiting workspace with application flow, candidate mix, open roles, and recent applicants.
examples.title: Talent Acquisition Command Center

examples.description: A clean project-controlling canvas modeled after the white-and-blue reference, with precise status cards and earned-value visuals.
examples.expected: Summary values use first-row semantics, monthly curves remain ordered, and cost composition traces back to cost-category rows.
examples.limitations: The example represents one selected project; use a report slicer or external filter to select other projects in Power BI.
examples.summary: Project identity, commercial KPIs, earned-value gauges, development curves, and cost composition.
examples.title: Capital Project Controls

examples.description: Combines the warm Productly visual language with portable semantic charts and a practical order work queue.
examples.expected: Monthly revenue, category share, recent orders, and upcoming payments all resolve from logical views over one sparse retail dataset.
examples.limitations: The balance card is illustrative and does not initiate payments or connect to a financial institution.
examples.summary: A coral-and-navy retail dashboard with revenue trends, category mix, order detail, and settlement reminders.
examples.title: Retail Sales Operations

examples.description: Adapts the compact violet mobility reference into a responsive Power BI map dashboard with analytical selection.
examples.expected: Map points fit the dataset, status legend selection links to other components, and route summaries retain contributing Power BI row identities.
examples.limitations: Street tiles require the Maps PBIVIZ profile, declared OpenStreetMap WebAccess, and network access in the host.
examples.summary: A map-first fleet workspace with live status, demand, battery health, usage trend, and busy-route detail.
examples.title: Urban Mobility Command Center

examples.description: Translates the airy blue-and-mint healthcare reference into a safe, accessible operational workspace.
examples.expected: Patient-level data drives aggregate KPIs, daily and departmental charts, and a selectable active-patient work queue.
examples.limitations: All people and clinical events are synthetic; the dashboard is not intended for diagnosis or real patient decisions.
examples.summary: A calm clinical operations dashboard for alerts, patient demand, review mix, department load, and response queues.
examples.title: Patient Care Operations

examples.description: Captures the midnight Paycent reference with neon accents and a safe CSS-rendered card that works offline.
examples.expected: Account summary values, monthly debit/credit activity, category spending, and recent transactions render responsively from one source.
examples.limitations: The payment card is a decorative dashboard element and never exposes or processes real card credentials.
examples.summary: A responsive dark banking workspace with balance cards, transaction history, spending mix, and account detail.
examples.title: Digital Banking Overview

examples.description: Blends the coral-framed monitoring reference and the dense website KPI wall into one practical growth dashboard.
examples.expected: Summary metrics, daily trends, medium performance, bounce gauge, and live-location list render from explicit logical record types.
examples.limitations: Location data is shown as a portable ranked list; this Core-profile example intentionally avoids external map tiles.
examples.summary: A dark editorial command board combining media monitoring with website conversion, engagement, and audience KPIs.
examples.title: Media & Web Performance

examples.description: Represents the futuristic HUD references using safe ECharts options and sanitized inline SVG rather than external raster artwork.
examples.expected: Summary gauges, topology, ordered multiseries telemetry, and grouped node-health records render without network access.
examples.limitations: The topology is a schematic network map; advanced 3D surfaces and geographic basemaps are intentionally omitted from the Core package.
examples.summary: A deep-teal telemetry wall with neon gauges, network topology, waveform analysis, and node health.
examples.title: Industrial Network Telemetry

examples.description: A synthetic water distribution network pairs inline station geometry with on-demand pressure telemetry, operating assignments, and maintenance notes.
examples.expected: Click each station to load different pressure readings. Hover or zoom its chart, expand the popup, page through the measurements, or refresh the station data.
examples.limitations: The local CSV is synthetic. Live details require HTTPS access to the public MiniUp Function. In Power BI, the Maps package and runtime WebAccess permission are required.
examples.summary: Three Houston pressure stations open interactive, live API analytics in map popups.
examples.title: Dynamic GIS Analytics

examples.description: A maintenance dispatcher browses a local asset queue while a responsive side panel and workload card fetch their component trees from MiniUp.
examples.expected: Select P-204 or another asset to load its work plan in the side panel. Select High under Work priority to query the filtered workload, then click Refresh workload to repeat the live request.
examples.limitations: The local CSV is synthetic. Live details require HTTPS access to the public MiniUp Function. In Power BI, the Maps package and runtime WebAccess permission are required.
examples.summary: Select a work order to open its live details, and query workload independently by priority.
examples.title: Universal Dynamic Content
examples.useCase: Maintenance dispatch and asset work orders

examples.description: Northbank Water's fictional booster station pairs four selectable centrifugal pump assemblies with pressure vessels, suction and discharge manifolds, and synthetic operating records. The spatial view, station KPIs, pressure trend, motor-load chart, and snapshot register all use the same source data.
examples.expected: Choose Peak demand to flag P-103 and start the standby pump, or Maintenance to stop P-102. Select equipment in the scene or its keyboard-accessible list to filter the trend, motor-load chart, and register. Select a motor-load bar or snapshot row to highlight its pump. Select the same asset again or clear the scene selection to restore the linked views. All uses the newest snapshot for station KPIs and asset status and averages pressure across the available scenarios.
examples.limitations: The three operating scenarios are precomputed snapshots. The project works offline and uses procedural equipment geometry. In Power BI, include readingid as a categorical column and set numeric fields to Don't summarize to preserve distinct reading rows. Configure Power BI visual interactions to test the selected rows against a second visual.
examples.summary: Explore a 3D booster station, rehearse changing duty conditions, and trace each pump to its operating history.
examples.title: Pump Station Monitoring
examples.useCase: Water utility operations and equipment telemetry

examples.description: Ridgeway Water's fictional network collects raw groundwater from a local well and a remote well, treats it at the groundwater plant, and pumps it through a distribution main to Maple Court, Cedar Lane, and Birch Grove. The scene uses distinct pipe colors and direction markers, with operating readings for all seven selectable assets.
examples.expected: Choose Remote well offline to see the source shut down and residential deliveries drop. Choose Peak demand to see the two wells support higher delivery. Select equipment or a house to filter the charts and asset register. Select a bar or register row to highlight its asset. All uses the latest snapshot for the station KPIs and averages the flow history across available readings.
examples.limitations: The site is a synthetic schematic and pipe geometry indicates direction. Readings are illustrative and do not simulate a hydraulic model. Import readingid in Power BI and set numeric columns to Don't summarize to preserve row identities.
examples.summary: Follow water from two wells through treatment and high-service pumping to three residential delivery points.
examples.title: Groundwater Supply & Distribution
examples.useCase: Groundwater treatment and residential water distribution
